title: Service Discovery
subtitle: A registry replaces hard-coded addresses, and you must choose whether it prefers stale answers or none
motto: Ask who is alive, do not remember where they used to be
keyInsight: A registry shrinks the time callers use a dead instance from a human's response time to a few missed heartbeats, but its own failure mode, AP or CP, decides what breaks when it does.

decisions.title: Compare a CP and an AP registry under the same outage
decisions.description: Frames three and four run one registry outage two ways, so the difference is the consistency choice and nothing else.
decisions.alternatives: Describing AP and CP in words alone would not show that stale entries cost far fewer requests than a blind registry.

decisions.title: Use heartbeat time as the detection cost
decisions.description: The detection window is the heartbeat interval times the missed beats, so the slider trades registry traffic against how long dead instances stay listed.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed detection time would hide the trade between chatty heartbeats and stale entries.
